metadata.project: King Follett Discourse — digital critical edition
metadata.description: The four eyewitness reports of the discourse of 7 April 1844 and the derived Times and Seasons composite (T), their reporters' roles that day, and the counts and page ranges derived from the transcripts. 'kind' is 'eyewitness' or 'derived'. word_count_raw counts whitespace-separated tokens of the raw body (JSP markup included); word_count_reading counts them in the reading rendering (kf.jsp.render_reading), which drops cancelled words, editorial glosses, page markers and footnote anchors. Page labels are as JSP gives them; brackets mark JSP-supplied pagination.
metadata.occasion: Funeral sermon for King Follett, preached in a grove east of the Nauvoo temple during the church's April 1844 general conference.
metadata.related_account: A polished account amalgamating Bullock's and Clayton's notes appeared in the Times and Seasons, 15 Aug. 1844. It is not one of the four witnesses collated here, but JSP footnotes cite it frequently; see kind 'times_and_seasons' in data/footnotes.json.

witnesses.title: Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Thomas Bullock
witnesses.document: Thomas Bullock, Minutes, 6–9 Apr. 1844, pp. 14–22, in Historian’s Office, General Church Minutes, CHL; handwriting of Thomas Bullock.
witnesses.role: Conference reporter and clerk. Bullock attended the April 1844 conference specifically as a reporter and took down the discourse as JS spoke; his text stands in his minutes of the 6–9 April 1844 conference (Historian's Office, General Church Minutes), pp. 14–22.
witnesses.role_source: JSP Source Note and Historical Introduction, 'Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Thomas Bullock'
witnesses.jsp_citation: JS, Discourse, [Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 7 Apr. 1844]. Featured version inscribed [ca. 7 Apr. 1844] in Thomas Bullock, Minutes, 6–9 Apr. 1844, pp. 14–22; handwriting of Thomas Bullock; Historian’s Office, General Church Minutes, CHL.

witnesses.title: Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Wilford Woodruff
witnesses.document: Wilford Woodruff, Journal, vol. 5, 1 Jan. 1843–31 Dec. 1844, pp. [133]–[140], Wilford Woodruff, Journals and Papers, CHL; handwriting of Wilford Woodruff.
witnesses.role: Personal journal. Woodruff was apparently not assigned to take notes; he wrote his account into his own journal, probably from rough notes taken while JS spoke — he recalled in 1877 having written the sermon down “on the crown of his hat, standing in the congregation.” JSP judges the journal text a fair copy or refined version of those notes.
witnesses.taken_down: personal record, refined from notes taken while JS spoke
witnesses.role_source: JSP Source Note and Historical Introduction, 'Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Thomas Bullock'
witnesses.jsp_citation: JS, Discourse, [Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 7 Apr. 1844]. Featured version inscribed [ca. 7 Apr. 1844] in Wilford Woodruff, Journal, vol. 5, 1 Jan. 1843–31 Dec. 1844, pp. [133]–[140]; handwriting of Wilford Woodruff; Wilford Woodruff, Journals and Papers, CHL.

witnesses.title: Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Willard Richards
witnesses.document: Joseph Smith, Journal, 1842–1844, book 4, pp. [67]–[71], JS Collection, CHL; handwriting of Willard Richards.
witnesses.role: JS's private secretary and historian, and keeper of JS's journal. Richards recorded his account as JS spoke; JSP describes it as shorter, less detailed and at times cryptic.
witnesses.role_source: JSP Source Note and Historical Introduction, 'Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Thomas Bullock'
witnesses.jsp_citation: JS, Discourse, [Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 7 Apr. 1844]. Featured version inscribed [ca. 7 Apr. 1844] in JS, Journal, 1842–1844, bk. 4, pp. [67]–[71]; handwriting of Willard Richards; JS Collection, CHL.

witnesses.title: Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by William Clayton
witnesses.document: William Clayton, Minutes, 6–8 Apr. 1844, pp. 11–18, in Historian’s Office, General Church Minutes, CHL; handwriting of William Clayton.
witnesses.role: JS's private clerk. Clayton recorded his account as JS spoke; JSP notes that it ends abruptly and fails to record the last part of the discourse.
witnesses.role_source: JSP Source Note and Historical Introduction, 'Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Reported by Thomas Bullock'
witnesses.jsp_citation: JS, Discourse, [Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 7 Apr. 1844]. Featured version inscribed [ca. 7 Apr. 1844] in William Clayton, Minutes, 6–8 Apr. 1844, pp. 11–18; handwriting of William Clayton; Historian’s Office, General Church Minutes, CHL.

witnesses.title: Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Published in Times and Seasons
witnesses.document: “Conference Minutes,” Times and Seasons, 15 Aug. 1844, vol. 5, no. 15, pp. 612–617 (Nauvoo, Illinois).
witnesses.role: Not a report of the discourse but the published composite made from the reports. Thomas Bullock and William Clayton amalgamated their own notes into the version printed in the Times and Seasons of 15 August 1844, four months after the sermon and two months after JS's death. T is included so readers can see how the received text of the discourse was built; it must never be counted as a fifth independent witness to what was said, and its agreements with B and C are not independent confirmation.
witnesses.role_source: refs/reextraction-report.md, quoting the JSP bibliographical source note for 'Discourse, 7 April 1844, as Published in Times and Seasons'
witnesses.jsp_citation: JS, Discourse, [Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, 7 Apr. 1844]. Featured version published in “Conference Minutes,” Times and Seasons, 15 Aug. 1844, vol. 5, no. 15, 612–617. For more complete source information, see the source note for Letter to Isaac Galland, 22 Mar. 1839.
witnesses.notes: JSP supplies no editorial footnotes, cancellation spans or underline spans for this printed transcript, so footnotes.json has an empty entry for T and the expected markup counts are zero. The JSP transcript opens with the conference-minutes framing ('The president then arose...') rather than the first-person opening every eyewitness has, and closes 'I add no more. God bless you all. Amen.'
